neutral_facts.value: The accused and the victim were brothers involved in a land dispute. On the day of the incident, the accused abused the victim's son, who then returned home and complained to the victim. The victim went to the terrace of his house and summoned the accused. The accused and his son responded, and the accused became enraged, rushed downstairs, retrieved a gun, and opened fire, killing the victim and injuring others. The prosecution presented eyewitness accounts, medical evidence, and recovered weapons to support the case. The co-accused was acquitted due to lack of incriminating evidence.

prosecution_argument.value: The prosecution argued that the appellant had committed the offence under Sections 302 and 307 IPC, and that the evidence, including eye-witnesses and medical evidence, proved the case beyond doubt. They also contended that the co-accused's acquittal did not affect the appellant's guilt.

quotes.text: The eye-witnesses including the informant have offered a consistent, coherent and convincing narration thereof which docs not admit of any doubt of their trustworthiness.
The medical evidence reveals injuries on the deceased and the injured compatible with the weapon used. The charges levelled against the appellant thus have been proved beyond doubt.

defence_argument.value: The defence argued that the prosecution failed to prove the charge against the appellant, citing the acquittal of the co-accused and the family relationship of the witnesses as undermining their credibility. They also claimed that no case for murder or attempt was proved.

quotes.text: The learned Amicus Curiae has persuasively argued that the prosecution has utterly failed to prove the charge against the appellant which is patently deducible amongst others from the exoneration of the co-accused Harpartap...
The plea of their family relationship to discredit them does not commend for acceptance in the attendant facts and circumstances.

legal_principle_applied.value: The court applied the principle that the prosecution must prove the case beyond reasonable doubt, and that the acquittal of a co-accused does not affect the conviction of another accused.

quotes.text: The charges levelled against the appellant thus have been proved beyond doubt.
His acquittal, having regard to the state of evidence has no bearing on the inculpatory involvement of the appellant somuch so, that his conviction in isolation is sustainable.

sentencing_rationale.value: The sentence was reduced to the period already undergone due to the time elapsed since the incident, the appellant's uncontrollable fit of anger, and the lack of intent to eliminate any of those fired at.

quotes.text: On an overall consideration of the fact situation and also the time lag in between, the conviction of the appellant moderated to one under Section 304 Part 1 IPC and 307 IPC.
Considering the facts of the case in particular, it would meet the ends of justice, if the sentence for the offences is reduced to the period already undergone.

judicial_mitigating_factors.value: The court considered the time elapsed since the incident, the root cause of the incident, and the appellant's uncontrollable fit of anger which deprived him of self-control.

quotes.text: The occurrence is of the year 2004 and meanwhile twelve years have elapsed.
The facts do not commend to conclude that the appellant had the intention of eliminating any one of those fired at, though he had the knowledge of the likely fatal consequences thereof.

other_sentence_order.value: The appellant was ordered to be set at liberty forthwith, if not required to be detained in connection with any other case.

quotes.text: In this view of the matter, as a corollary, the appellant is hereby ordered to be set at liberty forthwith, if he is not required to be detained in connection with any other case.
